title: The facade multipart-uploads payloads above the elicited threshold and rounds-trip byte-equal
asA: developer uploading large payloads (attachments, generated reports, backups)
iWant: the facade to switch to multipart upload above the elicited threshold, and to abort in-flight multipart on failure
soThat: my consumer code stays shape-stable across sizes and I do not leave orphan multipart uploads behind

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the elicited multipart threshold at 8 MiB (ADR-2903 default), when putObject is called with a 10 MiB payload, then the facade switches to multipart-upload (initiate, part-upload, complete), the get returns byte-equal 10485760 bytes back, and an objectPut event fires with size 10485760 and timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the facade opened against a running S3-compatible engine, threshold=8 MiB
acceptanceCriteria.when: putObject(key, contentType, body=<10 MiB Buffer>) then getObject(key)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the getObject returns a body of exact size 10485760 with byte equality to the put payload; the events list contains one objectPut record with size=10485760; no ListMultipartUploads on the bucket surfaces an in-flight upload after completion

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a simulated part-upload failure mid-multipart (SIMULATE_PART_UPLOAD_FAIL fixture switch), when putObject is called with a 10 MiB payload, then the facade issues AbortMultipartUpload before propagating the error, and a subsequent ListMultipartUploads on the bucket surfaces zero in-flight uploads for the key.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the facade opened, threshold=8 MiB, SIMULATE_PART_UPLOAD_FAIL=true
acceptanceCriteria.when: putObject(key, contentType, body=<10 MiB Buffer>) rejects mid-upload
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rejection propagates to the caller; a probe-side ListMultipartUploads(prefix=key) returns zero uploads; no completed object appears at key

acceptanceCriteria.description: Multipart aborted on part failure. Given a multipart-upload with N parts where part K uploadPart returns a non-2xx (a mid-stream 5xx or client abort), when the uploader catches the failure, then it calls AbortMultipartUpload against the upload id, no CompleteMultipartUpload runs, no partial object survives at the target key, and the facade emits multipartAborted with { key, uploadId, failedPartNumber } on the event sink.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a multipart-upload with N parts where uploadPart K returns non-2xx
acceptanceCriteria.then: AbortMultipartUpload runs; no CompleteMultipartUpload runs; no partial object survives; multipartAborted fires with {key, uploadId, failedPartNumber}
